title.rendered: My Grace Is Sufficient: The Gospel For Today

excerpt.rendered: Paul prayed three times for the thorn to be removed. God said no — and gave him something better. Today’s devotional on 2 Corinthians 12:9 and the grace that is sufficient for whatever you are carrying.

content.rendered:
The Gospel For Today | Tuesday, April 28, 2026

📖 Today’s Scripture

“But he said to me, ‘My grace is sufficient for you, for my power is made perfect in weakness.’ Therefore I will boast all the more gladly about my weaknesses, so that Christ’s power may rest on me.”
— 2 Corinthians 12:9 (NIV) | ESV

📝 Today’s Message

Paul had asked God three times to remove a painful thorn. And God’s answer was not yes. It was not no. It was something better: My grace is sufficient for you.

Sufficient. The Greek word is arkei — enough, adequate, more than what is needed. God is not saying “hang in there, I’ll give you just barely enough to cope.” He is saying: My grace is the supply — and the supply is inexhaustible.

But there is something even more stunning here. God says His power is made perfect — brought to its full expression — in weakness. Not despite weakness. In it. Which means your weakness is not an obstacle to God’s power working through you. It is the very condition in which His power shows up most clearly.

Religion tells you to hide your weakness, overcome it, pretend it is not there. The Gospel says something completely different: bring it. “When I am weak, then I am strong” — 2 Corinthians 12:10. Not strong because the weakness went away. Strong because Christ’s power rests on the person who has stopped pretending they can do it in their own strength.

You do not need to have it all together before God can use you. His grace is the power — and it is sufficient. Right now. For exactly what you are facing.

🙏 Prayer

Father, I stop striving to overcome in my own strength. Your grace is sufficient — not my effort, not my willpower, not my performance. I bring You my weakness today and I receive Your power in exchange. Let Christ’s strength rest on me. Thank You that sufficient grace is already mine in Christ. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

🗣️ Declaration

God’s grace is sufficient for me today. His power is made perfect in my weakness — not when I have overcome it, but right now, in the middle of it. I bring my need to Him and receive His supply. Christ’s power rests on me. I am strong — not in myself, but in Him. His grace is enough. It has always been enough. It is enough today.
